questions.question: Which of following is a fundamental physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Time, mass, length, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, luminous intensity, and amount of substance are the base (fundamental) physical quantities in SI. Since temperature has a dedicated SI base unit (kelvin), it is a fundamental physical quantity.

questions.question: Which one of the following physical quantities is not a fundamental quantity?
questions.explanation: Work is a derived physical quantity (with dimensions M L² T−2M\,L²\,T^{-2}) rather than a fundamental (base) quantity.

questions.question: Which of the following group of physical quantity can be considered as a group of fundamental physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Momentum=Mass x velocity(Not a group of fundamental physical quantity) Velocity =DisplacementTime(Not a group of fundamental physical quantity) F=ma (Not a group of fundamental physical quantity) Time ,force ,Velocity is a group of fundamental physical quantity as they are not related to each other.

questions.question: Which of the following sets cannot enter into the list of fundamental quantities in any system of units ?
questions.explanation: A valid set of fundamental units must consist of dimensionally independent quantities. In particular, “velocity” already depends on length and time (v∼L T−1v L\,T^{-1}), so including it along with LL and TT does not add a new independent dimension. Therefore, the set length, time, and velocity cannot serve as a complete set of fundamental quantities in any system of units.

questions.question: Velocity is a derived physical quantity which depends on _____ fundamental quantities.
questions.explanation: Velocity is defined as displacement (length) per unit time, so it depends on 2 fundamental quantities (length and time).

questions.question: Which of the following graph is correct: n= magnitude of measurement & u= unit of measurement.
questions.explanation: We know a measured quantity QQ can be expressed as Q=n u = constant where nn is the numerical value (magnitude) and uu is the unit. For a constant QQ: n=Q/un = {Q}{u} shows nn is inversely proportional to uu.So a plot of nn (vertical axis) against uu (horizontal axis) is a rectangular‐hyperbola type curve (option A). n u=Qn\,u = Q is a constant.So a plot of n un\,u (vertical axis) versus uu (horizontal axis) is a horizontal line (option B).Likewise, a plot of n un\,u (vertical axis) versus nn (horizontal axis) is also a horizontal line (option C). Hence, all these graphs correctly depict relationships for Q=n uQ = n\,u.

questions.question: The unit of potential energy is
questions.explanation: Potential energy has dimension [M L² T−2][M\,L²\,T^{-2}]. In cgs, that is g cm2 s−2{g}\,{cm}²\,{s}^{-2}.Only “g (cm/s)²” matches g cm2s2{g}\,{{cm}²{{s}².

questions.question: The dimensions of pressure are
questions.explanation: Recall pressure=forcearea{pressure} = {{force}}{{area}}. Force{Force} has dimensions [MLT−2][M L T^{-2}], and area{area} has dimensions [L²][L²]. Therefore, pressure{pressure} has dimensions [MLT−2][L²]=[ML−1T−2]{[M L T^{-2}]}{[L²]} = [M L^{-1} T^{-2}].

questions.question: Which one has the dimensions different from the remaining three ?
questions.explanation: Work, torque, and energy each have dimensions [ML²T−2][M L² T^{-2}]. Power has dimensions [ML²T−3][M L² T^{-3}].

questions.question: The dimensions of power are
questions.explanation: Power is work done per unit time. Work (or energy) has dimensions [M L² T−2][M\,L²\,T^{-2}]. Dividing by time [T][T] gives [M L² T−3][M\,L²\,T^{-3}].

questions.question: Dimensional formula of velocity of sound is
questions.explanation: The velocity of sound is just a speed, and speed (or velocity) generally has dimensions lengthtime{{length}}{{time}}. Therefore, its dimensions are [M⁰ L T−1][M⁰\,L\,T^{-1}].

questions.question: Dimensional formula for torque is
questions.explanation: Torque = (force) × (perpendicular distance). Force has dimensions [M L T−2][M\,L\,T^{-2}], and distance [L][L]. Hence, torque has dimensions [M L T−2]×[L]=[M L² T−2].[M\,L\,T^{-2}] [L] = [M\,L²\,T^{-2}].

questions.question: The dimensional formula of focal length is
questions.explanation: It is length so its dimension formula is [M⁰ {~L}¹ T⁰]

questions.question: The dimensional formula for impulse is: (where impulse is product of mass and change in velocity)
questions.explanation: Impulse = mass × change in velocity = [M] [LT–1] = [MLT–1]

questions.question: A physical quantity has the dimensions [M¹ L² T^{-3}] . Which of the following could it represent?

The speed of light in a medium is v . The refractive index of the medium is n . If the dimensions of n are [M⁰ L⁰ T⁰] , which of the following is the correct dimensional formula for the speed of light v ?

questions.question: Match list I with List II: List-I List-II (a) Torque I. kgm−1s−2 (b) Energy density II. kgms−1 (c) Pressure gradient III. kgm−2s−2 (d) Impulse IV. kgm²s−2 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: a - IV, b - I, c - III, d - II
a - I, b - lV, c - III, d - I
a - IV, b - III, c - I, d - II
a - IV, b - I, c - II, d - III
questions.explanation: Step 1: Identify each quantity’s SI dimensions Torque = Force × distance ⇒ [M L T−2]×[L]=[M L² T−2][M\,L\,T^{-2}] [L] = [M\,L²\,T^{-2}] = kg m² s⁻². Energy density = Energy/Volume ⇒ [M L² T−2]/[L³]=[M L−1 T−2][M\,L²\,T^{-2}]/[L³] = [M\,L⁻¹\,T^{-2}] = kg m⁻¹ s⁻². Pressure gradient = Pressure/distance ⇒ [M L−1 T−2]/[L]=[M L−2 T−2][M\,L⁻¹\,T^{-2}]/[L] = [M\,L⁻²\,T^{-2}] = kg m⁻² s⁻². Impulse = Force × time ⇒ [M L T−2]×[T]=[M L T−1][M\,L\,T^{-2}] [T] = [M\,L\,T^{-1}] = kg m s⁻¹. Step 2: Match with given List-II kg m⁻¹ s⁻², kg m s⁻¹, kg m⁻² s⁻², kg m² s⁻². Hence: (a) Torque → (4) (b) Energy density → (1) (c) Pressure gradient → (3) (d) Impulse → (2). That is a–IV, b–I, c–III, d–II.

Thus, px Ay Tz=(Mx Lx T−x)(L2y)(Tz)=Mx Lx+2y T− x+z.p(x)\,A(y)\,T(z) = (M(x)\,L(x)\,T^{-x})(L²y})(T(z)) = M(x)\,L(x)+2y}\,T^{-\,x+z}. Equate exponents to match M¹L²T−2M¹ L² T^{-2}: x=1,x+2y=2  ⇒  1+2y=2  ⇒  y=12,(− x)+z=−2  ⇒  −1+z=−2  ⇒  z=−1.x = 1, x + 2y = 2 \;\; 1 + 2y=2 \;\; y=12, (-\,x) + z = -2 \;\; -1 + z = -2 \;\; z=-1. questions.explanation: Let the dimension of surface tension SS be expressed as S  ∼  Ex Vy Tz.S \;\; E(x)\,V(y)\,T(z). In base units: SS (surface tension) has dimensions [M T−2][M\,T^{-2}]. EE (energy) has dimensions [M L² T−2][M\,L²\,T^{-2}]. VV (velocity) has dimensions [L T−1][L\,T^{-1}]. TT has dimensions [T][T]. Hence, Ex Vy Tz=  (Mx L2x T−2x)⏟from Ex  ×  (Ly T−y)⏟from Vy  ×  (Tz)⏟from Tz=Mx  L2x+y  T−2x−y+z.E(x)\,V(y)\,T(z) =\; {(M(x)\,L²x}\,T^{-2x})}_{{from }E(x)\;\; {(L(y)\,T^{-y})}_{{from }V(y)\;\; {(T(z))}_{{from }T(z) = M(x)\;L²x+y}\;T^{-2x - y + z}. We match it to [M¹L⁰T−2][M¹ L⁰ T^{-2}]. Thus: x=1x = 1 (for the MM exponent to be 1), 2x+y=0  ⟹  2(1)+y=0  ⟹  y=−2,2x + y = 0 2(1) + y = 0 y = -2, −2x−y+z=−2  ⟹  −2(1)−(−2)+z=−2  ⟹  −2+2+z=−2  ⟹  z=−2.-2x - y + z = -2 -2(1) - (-2) + z = -2 -2 + 2 + z = -2 z = -2. Hence S  ∼  E¹ V−2 T−2,S \;\; E¹\,V^{-2}\,T^{-2}, which matches E V−2 T−2E\,V^{-2}\,T^{-2}.

(B) Asin⁡(ωt+kx)A ( t + kx) involves a sine function and dimensionless arguments, again beyond pure dimensional analysis. questions.question: The mass of a box measured by a grocer's balance is 2.3 {~kg} . Two gold pieces of masses 20.15 {~g} and 20.17 {~g} are added to the box. The total mass of the box is
questions.explanation: A quick way is to convert everything to grams and then apply significant‐figure rules for addition: Box mass: 2.3 kg=2300 g2.3\,{kg} = 2300\,{g}. Written as “2.3 kg” typically indicates 2 significant figures (though sometimes one might interpret it as 2.30 kg). Gold pieces: 20.15 g and 20.17 g (4 sig. figs each). Summation in grams: 2300 g+20.15 g+20.17 g=2340.32 g.2300\,{g} + 20.15\,{g} + 20.17\,{g} = 2340.32\,{g}. When converting back to kilograms, that is 2.34032 kg2.34032\,{kg}. However, we cannot quote more significant figures than the least‐precise measurement (the box, at 2 sig. figs). Rounding to 2 sig. figs in kilograms gives 2.3 kg2.3\,{kg}. Looking at the answer choices: (A) 2.3 kg has the correct number of significant figures (2 sig. figs) given the original “2.3 kg” reading. (B), (C), (D) all show more decimal places (thus more sig. figs) than justified by the box measurement. Hence, the best way to report the total mass (to the proper significant figures) is 2.3 kg.{2.3\,{kg}.}

questions.question: Assertion (A): Special functions such as trigonometric, logarithmic and exponential functions are not dimensionless.Reason (R): A pure number, ratio of similar physical quantities, such as angle and refractive index, has no dimensions.
options: Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true; Reason (R) is a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true; Reason (R) is not a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) states that special functions (trig/log/exponential) “are not dimensionless.” Actually, standard treatment in physics shows that the arguments of these special functions must be dimensionless for the expressions to be valid. Moreover, sine, exponential, and logarithmic outputs are also taken as pure numbers (dimensionless) if their arguments are pure numbers. Therefore, the assertion as stated is false. Reason (R) states that a pure number (ratio of similar quantities, e.g., angle, refractive index) has no dimension. This is a well‐known fact: such ratios are dimensionless. Hence, the reason is true. Comparing both statements, the correct choice is: Assertion (A) is false, Reason (R) is true.

questions.question: The numbers 2.745 and 2.735 on rounding off to 3 significant figures will give:

Truncating at three digits: 2.73; next digit is ‘5’. The preceding digit ‘3’ is odd, so we increase it by 1. Hence 2.735 → 2.74. Therefore, both become 2.74, 2.74.

Symbolically, ΔPP  ≤  3 Δaa+  2 Δbb+  Δcc+  Δdd. P/P \;\; 3\, a/a +\;2\, b/b +\; c/c +\; d/d. Substitute the given percentage errors: 3×1%  +  2×2%  +  1×3%  +  1×4%=3+4+3+4=14%.31\% \;+\; 22\% \;+\; 13\% \;+\; 14\% = 3 + 4 + 3 + 4 = 14\%.

questions.question: The temperature of two bodies measured by a thermometer are t1 = [20 °C ± 0.5 °C] and t2 = [50 °C ± 0.5 °C]. The temperature difference and the error there in is;
questions.explanation: 1. Difference: Δt=t2-t1=50-20=30 °C. 2. Error propagation (addition/subtraction): Δ(Δt)=Δt1+Δt2=0.5+0.5=1 °C. Hence the temperature difference is 30±1 °C.

The velocity of projection of a body is increased by 2%. Other factors remaining unchanged, what will be the percentage change in the maximum height attained?
questions.explanation: For a projectile under the same angle of projection, the maximum height HH is proportional to v²v². So if vv increases by 2%, HH will increase by approximately 2×2%=4%2 2\% = 4\%. Hence the correct answer is 4%.

questions.question: In the given figure zero error will be?
questions.explanation: A quick rule of thumb for a screw gauge (or similar instrument) is: If the circular scale’s zero lies below the reference line when the instrument should read zero thickness, the instrument is reading more than zero → positive zero error. If the circular scale’s zero lies above the reference line, the instrument is reading less than zero → negative zero error. From the figure, the zero of the circular scale is above the main‐scale reference line, indicating a negative zero error.

questions.question: The pitch of a screw gauge is 0.5 mm and there are 100 divisions on it circular scale. The instrument reads +2 divisions when nothing is put in-between its jaws. In measuring the diameter of a wire, there are 8 divisions on the main scale and 83rd division coincides with the reference line. Then the diameter of the wire is
questions.explanation: Least Count: LC=pitchnumber of divisions=0.5 mm100=0.005 mm.{LC} = {{pitch}}{{number of divisions}} = {0.5\,{mm}}{100} = 0.005\,{mm}. Zero Error: Zero reading=+2 divisions  ⟹  zero error=+2×0.005=+0.010 mm.{Zero reading} = +2{ divisions} {zero error} = +2 0.005 = +0.010\,{mm}. (A positive zero error is subtracted from the final reading.) Measurement: Main scale: 8×0.5 mm=4.0 mm.8 0.5\,{mm} = 4.0\,{mm}. Circular scale: 83×0.005 mm=0.415 mm.83 0.005\,{mm} = 0.415\,{mm}. So raw diameter = 4.0+0.415=4.415 mm.4.0 + 0.415 = 4.415\,{mm}. Correct Diameter: =4.415 mm−0.010 mm=4.405 mm.= 4.415\,{mm} - 0.010\,{mm} = 4.405\,{mm}.

questions.question: A screw gauge gives the following readings when used to measure the diameter of a wire Main scale reading : 0 mm Circular scale reading : 52 divisionsGiven that 1 mm on main scale corresponds to 100 divisions on the circular scale. The diameter of the wire from the above data is:
questions.explanation: Step 1. Identify the pitch and least count If “1 mm on the main scale corresponds to 100 divisions on the circular scale,” then the pitch is 1 mm per revolution. Hence, the least count (LC) = (pitch) ÷ (number of circular divisions) = 1 mm ÷ 100 = 0.01 mm = 0.000 01 m. In centimeters, 0.01 mm = 0.001 cm. Step 2. Compute the reading Main scale reads 0 mm ⇒ 0.0 cm. Circular scale reads 52 divisions. Each division is 0.001 cm, so total reading = 52 × 0.001 cm = 0.052 cm. Hence, the diameter of the wire is 0.052 cm .

questions.question: Statement-I: A screw gauge having a smaller value of pitch has greater accuracy.Statement-II: The least count of screw gauge is directly proportional to the number of divisions on circular scale.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct & Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect & Statement-II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I: “A screw gauge having a smaller pitch has greater accuracy.” Since Least Count = (pitch) / (number of circular divisions), a smaller pitch (for the same number of divisions) means a smaller least count, hence greater accuracy. So Statement I is correct. Statement II: “The least count of screw gauge is directly proportional to the number of divisions on the circular scale.” In fact, LC = (pitch) / (number of divisions), so it is inversely proportional to the number of divisions on the circular scale. Thus, Statement II is incorrect. Therefore, the correct option is: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect.
